headline: The three standing questions about how this lane works are settled and written into the repo. Finished assembler work now goes up without asking, and the language the game is written in is mine to design with you agreeing to each addition before it lands.

headline: The freezing tool can no longer guess which copy of the engine it froze - it refuses to run without one, and records the answer.

Every future snapshot names its source, so the question 'are we testing against the right thing?' stops being a person reading a sentence. The 166 old records are deliberately left as they are: reconstructing their answers from prose would put a guess into the one file whose whole value is that it contains no guesses.

headline: A safety catch I designed would have jammed the moment it was needed most. The engine lane spotted it before it shipped, and it is fixed.
matters: Reference bytes for the game were twice frozen without this repo's real test suite ever running, and a wrong number rode along unnoticed. I am building the enforcement so that cannot happen quietly again. My first design had a trap: if a freeze failed its tests for a reason that needed a second freeze to fix, the first one could never be signed off - and the only ways out were to hand-edit the record or to sign off something that had not passed. Those are precisely the two things the catch exists to prevent, so it would have taught people to do the wrong thing at the exact moment it mattered. The fix lets a failed freeze be formally set aside instead, but only by actually doing the replacement, so it cannot become a shortcut. Separately, the engine lane answered the question I could not: the signature has to record how many of the strict checks actually ran, because that is the one number a suite run WITHOUT the strict flag cannot produce - and a suite without the flag is otherwise fully green and indistinguishable.
detail: REFREEZE-NEEDS-STRICT, branch feat/refreeze-attest, not yet landed. Original sketch: per-entry attestation on provenance.toml Entry, two-valued (attested/absent), enforcement on entry N+1 while N unattested, self-disarming ratchet mirroring aeon_rev, boundary derived from the chain never pinned to an entry number. Aeon (aeon-f2) refuted the two-valued shape: a freeze whose strict run legitimately fails is permanently unattestable, so a byte-moving fix requiring freeze N+1 deadlocks the chain with hand-editing or a false attestation as the only exits. Adopted their three-valued state: attested / absent / superseded-abandoned, where abandoned REQUIRES naming the successor entry so it is only reachable by performing the next freeze. Ruled here under this lane's standing autonomy on assembler internals rather than escalated to the hub. Also adopted their attestation contents: (1) sigil SHA + aeon_rev, (2) golden CRC32s read from the blobs at run time not copied from the entry, (3) count/names of strict-gated bodies that executed - the only value a non-strict run structurally cannot produce, since strict_gate() early-returns those bodies and a non-strict suite is fully green. Parts 1-2 stop reuse, part 3 stops vacuity. Per-field audit question given to the agent: 'could this value be right if the run never happened?' Ship condition: poison with SIGIL_STRICT_GATE unset must refuse the attestation or record zero strict bodies. Aeon released the hub's HOLD-THEN-LAND on their own account (they run strict before pushing, so chain 172 is attestable), so it lands after their 172 pushes rather than in the morning. Precedent chains: 169 c8e87ecb, 170 174f4300; stale constant SFX_BODY_LEN 2046 vs region 0x8DA=2266.

headline: Four numbers describing the cartridge's own size had quietly gone wrong, and the one that fooled the search was the one that looked most correct.
matters: These are the figures that say how long each build of the game is. Nothing in the project read them any more, so nothing could notice when they drifted - one was right the day it was typed and wrong within a month, and it stayed wrong for 28 days. The search that found them was looking for numbers typed in by hand, so it missed a fourth that was written as a NAME instead of a number: it looked like the computer had worked it out, and it hadn't - it was the wrong build's figure. The fix removes the stored numbers entirely, so the game works them out fresh every time and there is nothing left to go stale. There is now a check that would have caught all four.
detail: OFFCANON-ROT, merged at 959958c7 (via 731af546). Four off-canonical assembled_len values in native.rs: demo 0x11224 vs 0x1121c (+0x8), config_b 0x434d0 vs 0x8b6f0, config_a 0x5f65a vs 0xa7e70, and lean_profile spelled `pins::ASSEMBLED_LEN` (the canonical shape's bar, +0x1082 past lean's own). The fourth was invisible to a sweep enumerating large hex literals - 'a wrong value spelled as a symbol looks derived'. config_b's 0x434d0 was correct when typed 2026-07-30 (94768171). Stored field deleted; assembled_len() derives per call and panics rather than substituting. New gate crates/sigil-harness/tests/offcanon_assembled_bar.rs, 4 tests, source-only so it never skips; agent corrected its own overstatement - cross-tool for the canonical pair, temporal for the off-canonical five. REGION_A_LMA deleted: dead AND wrong (0x3DE vs derived 0x3D6). Suite 3947/0/4 = 3951 declared, zero skip:, zero ratchet:, clippy clean, AEON_DIR=.sigil-ref-353aaa49@353aaa49, log .sigil-verify-landing-b.log.

headline: We now know how much of the game's code the timing model can actually speak about - and measuring it turned up two ways the model can hand back a confident wrong number.
matters: The emulator lane was waiting on this figure. The answer depends entirely on how you count, so it is reported two ways rather than one, and the gap between them is itself the finding. More useful than the headline number: of the game's routines, about one in six could carry a timing budget and exactly one does. The two defects are the kind worth having found early - the timing built-in never checks which of the console's two processors it is on, so on the main chip it can hand back a figure measured in the other chip's clock units; and the sound-side adder tops out instead of refusing, returning its ceiling as though it were an answer. Neither can be reached by today's code, both by luck rather than design. Nothing is fixed yet; they are written down with the conditions that would close them.
detail: CYCLE-FRACTION, merged at 959958c7 (via 88a95ad9). Note docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-27-cycle-fraction.md; tool crates/sigil-harness/src/bin/cycle_fraction.rs, in no suite. Measured over all seven shipped_shapes at aeon 353aaa49. By instruction site: 68000 66.88% exact / 33.07% ceiling / 0.04% unmodeled; Z80 72.89% / 0 / 27.11%; combined 68.08/26.48/5.43. By proc worst-bucket: combined 12.22/64.53/23.25 - the ~7x divergence reconciles to 98% of the 68000 ceiling bucket being the linker-relaxation ruling, not data dependence (only 0.65% of 68000 instructions vary with operand values). Layer B: 63/357 (17.6%) 68000 procs and 10/142 (7.0%) Z80 procs could carry @budget; 1 does. Four brief corrections upheld: model is four-valued not three (Branch pairs); 'cannot time' is two different things (five unreachable trap #0 vs a deliberate Z80 demand subset); shipped_shapes() misses the seam-1 resident sound blob entirely (registry walk sees zero Z80 in every sound-on shape); Layer A/B is the axis, not the denominator. Defects ledgered: eval_cycles has no CPU dispatch (builtins.rs contains zero 'cpu' refs; verified firsthand) - a 68000 nop returns Z80 T-states, all 24 call sites are (cpu: z80) today; z80_cycles::span_cost accumulates u16 saturating_add, returns 65535 where it owes a refusal, ~20x headroom. Queued as CYCLES-CPU-GUARD and SPAN-COST-WIDTH. Clippy type_complexity fixed at desk in 959958c7 (aliases only).

headline: The check that was supposed to catch tests quietly opting out could never have failed - it was reading output the test runner throws away.
matters: Before a batch of the game's reference bytes is accepted, this repo runs its tests and requires that none of them quietly opted out. That requirement has been part of the ritual for a long time and it has never once been able to fail: the test runner hides the output of any test that passes, so the warning line it was looking for was always discarded before anyone could grep for it. Every landing that reported 'none opted out' - including two of mine tonight - was reporting on an empty page. It took one word on the command line to fix. The automated nightly check already had that word and was never blind, so the damage is bounded to hand-run landings. Separately, 30 tests across 11 files worded their opt-out in ways the check could not match even with the output visible; those now share one spelling, defined in one place, with a lint that fails if a new one drifts.
detail: Verified firsthand before acting: same binary, `cargo test --release -p sigil-cli --test seam2_dac_emit` gives 0 skip-shaped lines, `-- --nocapture` gives 2. libtest captures passing tests' stdout/stderr. OVERSEER.md bar at :320 now carries `-- --nocapture` INSIDE the command span (bar 25 corrective 2). scripts/nightly_source_gates.sh:262 already passed it - so the earlier claim that the automated backstop 'shares the ritual's blind spot' is true for the SPELLING and false for CAPTURE; corrected in the doc. SKIP-TEXT-HOLE landed at c1718cb2 (via df21c18f): brief said 27 sites/9 files, measured 30 code paths/11 files - +2 in seam2_colink_probe.rs spelling `skip ` with a space, +1 in resumable.rs with no skip vocabulary at all and NOT strict-gated. The reported 176 `skip:` was a raw literal grep incl. doc comments; actual announcement sites 136 -> 166. SKIP_MARKER now defined once in test_support.rs and EXTRACTED by sed in the nightly script (exit 2 if unextractable). New gate skip_marker_lint, 2 tests, 6 poisons each red-then-restored, in SOURCE_GATES (40). Suite 3950/0/4 = 3954 declared, cross-checked by `cargo test --workspace -- --list` = 3954 (different enumeration parameter). clippy exit 0, audit unclassified=0, marker hits 0 with capture OFF.

headline: A landing gate I wrote would have taken the nightly safety net dark on its first night, by tripping the exact alarm it was built to restore.
matters: The new lint prints a one-line summary saying all the opt-out warnings are correctly worded - and that summary quoted the warning text itself. The nightly check greps the log for that text and shuts the whole lane down when it finds it, on the assumption that a test went quiet. So a perfectly healthy run of the new gate would have looked exactly like the failure it exists to detect, every night, starting the first. It only surfaced because I had just fixed the blindness above; with the old command the line was invisible and it would have shipped. The gate now describes the warning instead of printing it, and refuses to run if its own summary ever contains it again.
detail: Caught at landing on branch fix/skip-text-hole. The census used `{SKIP_MARKER:?}` which renders `"skip: "`; nightly_source_gates.sh does `grep -qF "$SKIP_MARKER" "$OUT"` -> note COULD NOT RUN, exit 2, whole lane dark. Confirmed by running the nightly's own extraction+grep against the green log: 1 match, the census line. Fixed at 0ce85540: census says 'the canonical marker', plus `assert!(!census.contains(SKIP_MARKER))` with a diagnostic naming the rendered line. Proven red-first by restoring the interpolation - fails at skip_marker_lint.rs:308 quoting the exact string - then restored and re-verified green. Note the shape: this is the parcel's own subject (a check that reports nothing reads as a check that found nothing) turned back on the parcel, and the ONLY reason it was visible is the --nocapture fix landed minutes earlier.

headline: Nine hand-typed cartridge addresses in the test suite were all wrong, and one of the tests they sat in was proving nothing whatsoever.
matters: These tests deliberately damage the game's data and check the bytes come out different. Nine of them had the address typed in by hand, and all thirteen numbers were out of date. Eight still did their job by luck. The ninth did not: it was looking in the release build for data that only exists in the debug build, so the bytes it wanted were not there whether or not the test damaged anything - it would have passed no matter what broke. It now reads the debug build and has a second arm that fails if the undamaged version stops matching. The proof this was fixed the right way rather than merely re-typed: three of the nine addresses moved again during the session, and the suite passed across that with no edits at all.
detail: STALE-PROBE-BASES landed at c1718cb2 (via 1087a139/6f1aa514/2ea69be5). Nine sites, thirteen literals, across tranche{2,4,5,6}_negative_probes.rs; all thirteen differed from their pins; all ruled INPUT (lma_base fed to place_sections), none an oracle - contrast native_full_rom.rs:180 where repin generates the pin from the listing convsym resolves, genuinely circular. My 'not load-bearing' characterisation REFUTED for the ninth: doctored_af_delete_produces_different_bytes sliced s4.bin but PARTICLE_ANIMS is DEBUG-only (plain_len==0); the bytes 00 02 04 02 02 02 FB 00 occur nowhere in s4.bin's 718,999 bytes and exactly once in s4.debug.bin. Vacuous, not merely stale. Also found: the region `size` beside each base is hand-typed too, 7 of 8 disagreed (ledgered, no gate). New gate probe_base_hygiene.rs keyed on region NAME so no allowlist, 60 blocks covered; 5 poisons, one came back GREEN revealing a real per-line marker hole that blanket-cleared every region on a line - hardened, now red at vectors_port.rs:327. Regions that moved mid-session: particle_anims 0x2ac78->0x2aca8, sonic_anims 0x29ff0->0x2a020, act_descriptor 0x16764->0x16794.
